finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after only a weak hostname check. `host.endswith("example.com")` has no leading dot, so it accepts any host that merely ends with that string, such as `attackerexample.com` or `evil-example.com`. The unused `ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com"` shows the dot was intended. An attacker can register such a domain, or point its DNS at 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or an internal IP, and have the server request internal resources. The scheme, port and resolved IP are not restricted, and the hostname is resolved again at connect time, so DNS rebinding also works. Only the response length is returned, so the impact is a blind or semi-blind SSRF that still allows internal port scanning and triggering internal endpoints. httpx does not follow redirects by default, which limits redirect-based bypasses.

trace.note: `url: str` comes straight from the request query string
urlparse(url).hostname is extracted, or "" if absent
Check is `host.endswith("example.com")`. It has no dot boundary, so `evilexample.com` and `attacker-example.com` pass. No scheme, port or IP check, and no DNS pinning.
The original raw `url` string, not the parsed value, is passed to httpx.get. httpx re-parses it with its own parser, and the hostname is resolved again at connect time.

finding.guards_checked: Checked the endswith("example.com") hostname check, which is bypassable because it lacks the leading dot. ALLOWED_SUFFIX is defined but never used. There is no scheme allow-list, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no connect-time address validation. httpx follows no redirects by default, so redirects are not an extra bypass. /ping uses a constant URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary; does not close the finding). ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and reaches `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) behind only the bypassable `endswith("example.com")` check at mirror.py:13, with no auth, scheme or IP restriction in the file.
